articles.title: Mortes decorrentes de intervenção policial voltam a crescer na gestão Tarcísio e atingem maior número desde 2020 na cidade de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: SSP afirmou que atua com foco na preservação da vida, na revisão de protocolos, no uso de tecnologias e no combate a desvios de conduta.
articles.summary: SSP afirmou que atua com foco na preservação da vida, na revisão de protocolos, no uso de tecnologias e no combate a desvios de conduta.
articles.body:
O número de mortes decorrentes de intervenção policial na cidade de São Paulo voltou a crescer durante a gestão Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) e atingiu o maior patamar desde 2020.

Entre janeiro e setembro deste ano, foram registradas 191 mortes, segundo dados do Grupo de Atuação Especial da Segurança Pública e Controle Externo da Atividade Policial (Gaesp), do Ministério Público de São Paulo (MP-SP). Isto é, a média foi de uma morte a cada 34 horas em 2026.

Os dados incluem mortes provocadas por policiais em serviço e de folga. O total considera os nove primeiros meses de cada ano e mostra uma mudança na trajetória dos registros a partir de 2023, primeiro ano do governo Tarcísio.

Entre janeiro e setembro de 2020, foram contabilizadas 264 mortes. O número caiu para 178 em 2021 e chegou a 124 em 2022, último ano do governo Rodrigo Garcia (PSDB).

A partir de 2023, porém, os registros voltaram a subir ano a ano. Foram 141 mortes nos nove primeiros meses daquele ano, 176 em 2024, 188 em 2025 e 191 em 2026.

Na comparação entre 2022 e 2026, o aumento foi de 54%, de 124 para 191 mortes. Em 2026, a média foi de uma morte a cada 34 horas.

Mortes em decorrência de intervenção policial na cidade de São Paulo. — Foto: Arte/TV Globo

Duas ocorrências recentes na capital paulista terminaram com mortes durante abordagens policiais e dezenas de disparos de armas de fogo.

No sábado (10), Gustavo Munis de Santana, de 20 anos, foi morto com 27 tiros disparados por policiais militares durante uma abordagem em Moema, na Zona Sul da cidade. Segundo a polícia, o celular que ele segurava foi confundido com uma arma. Gustavo não tinha antecedentes criminais.

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, quatro policiais militares dispararam 45 vezes durante a abordagem. Familiares relataram à polícia que o jovem morava com a mãe e as irmãs e fazia tratamento com antidepressivos.

Outro caso ocorreu na madrugada de 3 de outubro, na Vila Dionísia, Zona Norte. Um vídeo gravado por testemunhas mostra policiais militares atirando ao menos 24 vezes contra Antonio Nunes Batista, de 40 anos, depois de ele cair no chão durante uma abordagem.

Segundo a versão apresentada pelos policiais no boletim de ocorrência, Antonio estava armado com uma faca e uma barra de ferro e ameaçava pedestres. Os agentes disseram que tentaram contê-lo com uma arma de eletrochoque, mas que a medida não foi suficiente. Ainda de acordo com os policiais, ele teria continuado a investida, o que levou três PMs a disparar.

As imagens, porém, mostram Antonio já caído quando os tiros começam. O boletim de ocorrência informa que nenhum dos policiais envolvidos utilizava câmera corporal.

Gustavo Munis de Santana, de 20 anos, atingido por 27 tiros de policiais militares em Moema. E Antonio Nunes Batista, de 40 anos, foi atingido por 24 tiros disparados por agentes no dia 3 de outubro. — Foto: Montagem/g1/Reprodução/TV Globo

Em nota enviada à TV Globo, a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP) afirmou que atua com foco na preservação da vida, na revisão de protocolos, no uso de tecnologias e no combate a desvios de conduta.

A pasta disse que a análise da letalidade policial considera o contexto de cada ocorrência, o volume de operações, o uso correto das armas e o cumprimento das regras para utilização de câmeras corporais.

Segundo a secretaria, toda morte decorrente de intervenção policial é investigada com rigor, com acompanhamento das corregedorias, do Ministério Público, do Poder Judiciário e de órgãos de controle externo.

articles.title: ‘Pistol to chest, bottle of petrol in hand’: BJP neta held hostage, robbed of Rs 12 lakh at Kanpur farmhouse
articles.summary: BJP Pichhda Morcha state secretary Ramesh Yadav was held hostage at his Kanpur farmhouse and robbed of Rs 12 lakh cash, jewellery and a watch; police probe on.
articles.body: KANPUR: Two masked men allegedly held BJP Pichhda Morcha state secretary Ramesh Yadav hostage at his farmhouse in Kanpur and robbed him of Rs 12 lakh in cash, jewellery and a watch on Monday night.The robbers tied his hands and legs, locked him in a bathroom and fled after spending about 37 minutes at the farmhouse in the Sen Paschimpara police station area, around 20 kilometres from the city.Yadav, who became Pichhda Morcha state secretary on Oct 1, had returned from Lucknow around 12.30 am after assuming charge. He was staying alone at the four-bigha farmhouse, about 500 metres from his home, where four guards were deployed.Yadav said his servant, Abhay Rajput, served him food and left around 10.45 pm. About 15 minutes later, two men entered, with one pressing a country-made pistol against his chest and the other carrying a bottle of petrol.They initially demanded Rs 2 crore before taking Rs 12 lakh from a locker and snatching his gold chain, ring and Rado watch, Yadav said. They then bound him tightly and left him with a towel and a water bottle. Yadav freed himself from the cello tape and called a guard, who rescued him.Police were informed at 1.20 am. Additional Police Commissioner Vipin Tada and DCP Deependranath Chaudhary inspected the scene.No CCTV footage showed the robbers entering the premises, but two men dressed in black were recorded fleeing by stepping on a washbasin and jumping over a tin shed. Police suspect they may have entered using a tree adjoining a room, where shoe-friction marks were found.Investigators said the robbers appeared familiar with the farmhouse. Police are examining details of visitors and questioning suspects. A dog squad traced a route from the garden and room to a field behind the boundary wall.Police commissioner Raghubir Lal said eight teams were investigating the case and two suspects were being questioned.The farmhouse has a 10-foot boundary wall topped with two feet of barbed wire and is equipped with 50 CCTV cameras.Yadav has served two terms as block pramukh and also unsuccessfully contested the 2022 assembly election from Bithoor on a BSP ticket.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kanpur | Silver Rate in Kanpur | Bank Holidays in Kanpur | Public Holidays in Kanpur | Kanpur AQI | Weather in Kanpur | Petrol Price in Kanpur | Diesel Price in Kanpur | CNG Price in Kanpur | LPG Price in KanpurStay updated with the latest Kanpur news. articles.title: FIR on IAS officer for attack on police at Bengaluru nightclub
articles.summary: AP-cadre IAS officer Vikas Marmat and three others booked in Bengaluru for allegedly abusing and assaulting cops during an underage liquor check; CM Naidu orders probe.
articles.body: BENGALURU: An Andhra Pradesh-cadre IAS officer and his realtor-friend were among the four booked on charges of abusing and attacking police officers at a nightclub on Residency Road in Bengaluru when the latter were checking the credentials of customers to ensure liquor was not served to underage customers.The 2019-batch officer under police scanner is Vikas Marmat, currently serving as project director of Kuppam Area Development Authority in AP chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu’s home constituency, Kuppam. His friends booked are Abhay Uday Singh, a real estate businessman and resident of Akshaynagar on Bannerghatta Road, and Nitish, owner of a competitive exams coaching centre and resident of Bihar. The fourth person booked is Roshan, a bouncer.While the officer has been named as primary accused, others were named co-accused in the incident that took place on the night of Oct 9. Next morning, Vikas and others apologised for their act, police said.The incident unfolded when sleuths from Central Crime Branch (CCB) visited Cavore on Residency Road as part of a drive to check underage revelry at liquor joints. A team led by inspector Arun Salunke visited the outlet around 1.30am. While interacting with revellers, a police officer asked a few young women to produce documents to prove age. This made Vikas and Abhay angry. They allegedly started behaving tersely with the police.“First, Vikas, saying he was an IAS officer, asked what rights we had to ask the girls to produce age documents. We replied stating this was part of a special drive against pubs and bars that serve liquor to minors. Then, Vikas asked under whose direction we were doing it. We replied that our police commissioner has directed it. Then, Vikas asked what’s our jurisdiction limit. We replied CCB covers the entire city. At this, Vikas became furious, saying no such powers have been given to police, where one branch can act anywhere in the city like Bengaluru. By then, he abused us. When we resisted, Abhay Uday Singh pushed and attacked us,” a cop present at the scene told TOI.Nitish and Roshan too allegedly abused and pushed other cops, asking them to go out. Vikas allegedly hurled expletives at the cops, which was videographed and the same went viral on Tuesday. Soon, more police force reached the place and all four men were taken to Cubbon Park police station.Police inspector Arun Salunke registered the FIR stating the four allegedly picked up an altercation, abused and attacked the cops on duty. Accordingly, police registered a case against Vikas, Abhay, Nitish and Roshan for criminal intimidation, assault on a public servant to prevent them from discharging their duties and use of criminal force to dishonour a person.CM Naidu orders probeFollowing demands by YSRCP, Andhra Pradesh chief minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu has directed the chief secretary to submit a detailed report on the incident. articles.title: Gwent Police considers 'zero-hours' detectives as murder investigations surge
articles.summary: The chief constable said the force had seen "unprecedented" demand in the past year.
articles.body:
An "unprecedented" number of murder investigations this year could see Gwent Police hire detectives on "zero-hour" style contracts to cope with demand.

Chief Constable Mark Hobrough said the force would normally see two or three murder probes a year, but has launched 11 in the past 10 months.

As a result it has had to fund record amounts of overtime payments and take neighbourhood officers away from community policing duties to cope with the demand.

Hobrough said the 1,535 officer-strong force would use the additional detectives if the same trend continues next year, but did not specify where they would come from or how the scheme would work.

Hobrough told Monmouthshire councillors that if demand continued he would consider cheaper alternatives to support investigations such as an "almost zero hours-type situation" to conduct interviews or special investigations outside the force's boundary.

"But that has to be of the same quality," he said, adding that he did not want to risk burnout among his staff.

He said: "They are the same people going to these incidents... They are young officers doing an outstanding job and I want to make sure we are looking after them and they stay with us long term."

The chief constable described one particular dog attack involving a baby as an "absolute tragedy", adding: "Our neighbourhood officers were the first on the scene, it's left trauma, it is bound to.

"They've been to the two murder scenes [in Monmouthshire] which were particularly harrowing incidents. It's about making sure we look after the teams, to support them and keep them in service and healthy and leave healthy."

Hobrough said in the last 10 months the force had dealt with the number of murders that would typically take place in two to three years.

"That is a huge extraction for officers," he said.

Hobrough stressed there was no link between the incidents, which involved factors ranging from alleged organised crime to mental health issues, substance misuse and domestic violence.

"There is no correlation between them at all," he said.

The force had also responded to public order protests outside its areas as part of an agreement to support deployments nationally, as well as helping the fire service as it tackled wildfires , Hobrough said.

He said that while neighbourhood officers had been "extradited" in response to the major demands during the first half of this year, their numbers were still at an "incredibly low" level.

"It's absolutely what we don't want," he said.

"Historically it used to be the go-to for community officers to staff response cars in a shortage, that isn't the case now," he said.

articles.title: ‘Ela tremia muito’: funcionária de posto acolheu menina salva de tentativa de estupro após fazer sinal universal de socorro em Curitiba | G1
articles.standfirst: Menina de 9 anos foi abordada a caminho da escola por homem que tentou levá-la à força. Primo reconheceu gesto de socorro e pediu ajuda em posto de combustíveis. Suspeito foi preso.
articles.summary: Menina de 9 anos foi abordada a caminho da escola por homem que tentou levá-la à força. Primo reconheceu gesto de socorro e pediu ajuda em posto de combustíveis. Suspeito foi preso
articles.body:
A gerente de pista de um posto de combustíveis, Josiane Rodrigues Aires, acolheu a menina de 9 anos salva de uma tentativa de estupro em Curitiba após ela fazer o sinal universal de socorro. Segundo Josiane, a criança tremia, chorava muito e perguntava se o suspeito voltaria ao local. Assista acima.

“Abracei tanto ela, quanto o priminho dela que estava nervoso. Choraram bastante. Ela tremia muito, e falava: ‘Ô, tia, ele tá vindo? Ele vai vir de novo?’ Eu falava: ‘Não, fica calma que ele não vai vir’. A preocupação dela era ele chegar perto de novo”, contou Josiane.

O caso aconteceu na manhã de sexta-feira (9), no bairro Sítio Cercado. A menina estava indo para a escola com outras crianças, entre elas o primo de 10 anos , quando foi abordada por um homem de 54 anos.

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, o suspeito ofereceu dinheiro para que ela o acompanhasse. Após a recusa, segurou a mão da criança à força e começou a conduzi-la. O suspeito não teve o nome divulgado.

Com medo, a única reação que a criança teve foi fazer o sinal de socorro, que consiste em dobrar o polegar para dentro da palma da mão e fechar os outros quatro dedos sobre ele.

Frentistas ajudaram a salvar menina de tentativa de estupro em Curitiba — Foto: Auto Posto Osternack

Ao reconhecer o gesto, o menino correu até um posto de combustíveis e pediu ajuda.

"Eu cheguei falando que o homem estava tentando roubar a minha prima. Eles já levaram a sério", lembra o menino.

Primo correndo para pedir ajuda, enquanto prima é levada por homem de 54 anos — Foto: Reprodução

Câmeras de segurança registraram o menino pedindo ajuda. Funcionários e clientes foram em direção ao suspeito, que fugiu. Os frentistas acionaram uma viatura da Guarda Municipal que passava pela região, e o homem foi preso em flagrante por tentativa de estupro de vulnerável.

Segundo a corporação, ele era monitorado por tornozeleira eletrônica desde 2017 por estupro de vulnerável.

Criança faz sinal universal de pedido de socorro e homem é preso por tentativa de estupro de vulnerável, em Curitiba — Foto: RPC

Os dois contaram à RPC , afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, as crianças contaram que aprenderam o significado do gesto após ver reportagens na televisão e conversar com a avó.

"Eu sabia [do sinal] pela TV e pela avó ensinar. Ela falou que, quando nós estivermos em perigo, é só fazer o sinal que daí as pessoas ajudam", detalha a menina.

A avó contou que costuma orientar os netos sobre como se proteger na rua, incluindo não conversar com estranhos nem aceitar doces ou dinheiro de desconhecidos.

Sinal de socorro usado por mulheres em situação de perigo — Foto: g1 PR

O sinal universal de socorro foi criado no Canadá. Uma agência de publicidade de Toronto desenvolveu, em abril de 2020, uma campanha com ações para conter o crescimento dos casos de violência doméstica registrados no período de confinamento da Covid-19. O intuito era criar um gesto simples e seguro que poderia ser utilizado por vítimas de violência doméstica para denúncias, sem que o agressor percebesse o pedido de socorro.

Segundo especialistas, ao perceber alguém fazendo o gesto, a orientação é tentar se aproximar da pessoa de forma discreta e amigável, como se conhecesse a vítima, e levá-la para um local seguro, como um comércio ou uma farmácia.

A recomendação é conversar com a vítima e encaminhá-la aos órgãos competentes, como a delegacia.

Se não for possível se aproximar, a orientação é procurar a polícia e relatar a situação.

articles.title: Câncer de pulmão do papa: veja perguntas e respostas sobre a saúde de Leão XIV | G1
articles.standfirst: Exame confirmou câncer após cirurgia para retirar parte do pulmão direito. O Vaticano não divulgou o estágio da doença nem se o papa precisará de outros tratamentos.
articles.summary: Exame confirmou câncer após cirurgia para retirar parte do pulmão direito. O Vaticano não divulgou o estágio da doença nem se o papa precisará de outros tratamentos.
articles.body:
O papa Leão XIV passou por uma cirurgia na terça-feira (13) para retirar um tumor do pulmão direito. O exame do tecido removido confirmou que o pontífice tem adenocarcinoma pulmonar , um tipo de câncer de pulmão.

Veja abaixo o que se sabe sobre o estado de saúde do papa.

Segundo o Vaticano , Leão XIV descobriu a lesão durante exames de rotina. Na missa do último domingo (11), o papa afirmou que o nódulo havia sido detectado em estágio inicial e que seu crescimento estava “bem controlado”.

Apesar disso, os médicos recomendaram a remoção cirúrgica. A declaração foi feita antes da confirmação do diagnóstico de câncer.

Papa Leão chega ao Hospital Gemelli antes da cirurgia para remoção de um nódulo pulmonar, em Roma 13 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Ciro de Luca

A cirurgia foi coordenada pelos médicos Stefano Margaritora, Elisa Meacci, Maria Teresa Congedo e Leonardo Petracca Caravella . Já a equipe de anestesiologia foi composta pelo professor Massimo Antonelli, e pelos doutores Giovanni Punzo e Giuseppe Bello.

A operação durou cerca de uma hora e meia e foi considerada bem-sucedida, sem complicações, segundo o Vaticano. Os médicos retiraram o lobo inferior do pulmão direito por meio de uma técnica videoassistida .

Leão XIV foi atendido no Hospital Universitário Agostino Gemelli, em Roma, na Itália . Inaugurado em 1964, o hospital é ligado à Universidade Católica do Sagrado Coração e é considerado uma das principais referências médicas do país.

A instituição é conhecida por atender papas. João Paulo II foi internado no local em 1981, após sofrer um atentado a tiros na Praça de São Pedro. O papa Francisco também recebeu tratamento no Gemelli, onde ficou internado por 38 dias para tratar uma pneumonia bilateral. Após receber alta, voltou à residência no Vaticano, onde passou as últimas semanas de vida .

É o tipo mais comum de câncer de pulmão . Ele se desenvolve em células que produzem muco e representa cerca de 40% dos casos, segundo o Instituto Nacional do Câncer (Inca). É mais frequente em fumantes, mas também pode atingir pessoas que nunca fumaram. Em alguns casos, o tumor apresenta alterações genéticas que permitem o uso de medicamentos específicos.

O tratamento do câncer de pulmão depende do tipo e do estágio do tumor, além das condições de saúde do paciente. Quando possível, a cirurgia é uma das principais opções. No caso de Leão XIV, os médicos retiraram o lobo inferior do pulmão direito, em um procedimento conhecido como lobectomia.

Dependendo da avaliação médica, o tratamento também pode incluir quimioterapia, radioterapia, imunoterapia ou medicamentos direcionados a alterações genéticas do tumor. Ainda não há informações sobre a necessidade de terapias adicionais para o pontífice.

O papa Leão XIV, nome adotado por Robert Francis Prevost, tem 71 anos e nasceu em 14 de setembro de 1955, em Chicago, nos Estados Unidos. Ele foi eleito em maio de 2025 , tornando-se o primeiro papa nascido no país. Antes de assumir o comando da Igreja Católica, atuou como missionário no Peru por vários anos, onde também obteve cidadania peruana.

Como está a saúde do papa de modo geral?

Antes do diagnóstico atual, Leão era conhecido por manter uma rotina de atividades físicas. Ele joga tênis regularmente e costuma nadar durante os períodos de descanso em Castel Gandolfo, na Itália.

Antes de ser eleito papa, frequentava a academia duas ou três vezes por semana, com treinos de cerca de uma hora, voltados principalmente à saúde cardiovascular e à postura. Não há informações públicas sobre outras doenças diagnosticadas.

Antes de assumir o pontificado, Leão XIV teve um episódio grave de saúde em 1985, quando contraiu febre tifoide aos 29 anos, durante sua atuação missionária no Peru. A doença marcou sua trajetória, e ele permaneceu no país, onde trabalhou por vários anos.

Na véspera da cirurgia, o papa cumpriu os sete compromissos previstos para a manhã no Vaticano.

Em entrevista ao National Catholic Reporter, John Prevost, irmão do papa, contou que a mãe dos dois morreu de câncer. Inicialmente, os médicos estimaram que ela viveria apenas seis meses, mas ela sobreviveu por vários anos após receber um medicamento experimental. Perto do fim da vida dela, Leão XIV permaneceu ao seu lado dia e noite para que não ficasse sozinha.

O pai do pontífice também morreu de câncer, cerca de sete anos depois da mãe. Outro irmão, Louis Prevost, de 74 anos, também está em tratamento contra a doença e estava internado na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos. Os tipos de câncer enfrentados por Louis e pelos pais não foram divulgados nos relatos.

As chances de recuperação diminuem significativamente à medida que o câncer avança.

O estágio do tumor do papa não foi divulgado. Essa informação é fundamental para estimar as chances de cura. A avaliação considera o tamanho do tumor, o comprometimento dos linfonodos e a presença de metástases, quando a doença se espalha para outros órgãos.

A análise do tecido retirado também pode revelar o perfil genético do tumor, informação que ajuda a orientar o tratamento.

articles.title: Renda média de R$ 87 mil e 25,9 mil perfis: Campinas tem um 'daddy' para cada 5 sugar babies | G1
articles.standfirst: Plataforma de relacionamento sugar reúne 228,7 mil usuários na cidade; biomédica de 24 anos relata viagens, presentes e oportunidades profissionais.
articles.summary: Plataforma de relacionamento sugar reúne 228,7 mil usuários na cidade; biomédica de 24 anos relata viagens, presentes e oportunidades profissionais.
articles.body:
Anel que Julia ganhou do noivo — Foto: g1

Um levantamento de uma plataforma de relacionamento sugar mostra que a renda média dos daddies de Campinas (SP) é de R$ 87,2 mil . Isso representa uma renda até 19 vezes maior que a valor médio dos salários na cidade , segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

De acordo com o MeuPatrocínio, são 25,9 mil daddies em um universo com 148,1 mil babies - média de 5,7 para cada daddy . Ao todo, a plataforma possui 228,7 mil inscritos no município de 1,1 milhão de habitantes.

🔍Em inglês, sugar baby significa "bebê de açúcar". A expressão nasceu nos Estados Unidos, no início do século 20, para definir a relação entre um homem mais velho e rico, o daddy (pai em inglês), que banca uma mulher jovem, a baby.

Em menor número, a plataforma também reúne sugar babies masculinos e sugar mommies em Campinas, esses sem informações da renda média declarada.

Os números de Campinas são um recorte da pesquisa feita pela plataforma com usuários em todo o Brasil. A empresa afirma que boa parte dos sugar daddies é formada por empresários, investidores e executivos, com idade média declarada de 39 anos .

Uma biomédica de 24 anos, que pediu para não ser identificada, afirma que encontrou nos relacionamentos sugar oportunidades e experiências que proporcionaram presentes, viagens e novas possibilidades profissionais.

Ela que se define como de uma família de classe média baixa, reconhece que muitos dos sonhos seriam difíceis de serem alcançados fora da plataforma.

"Nunca passei vontade de nada, mas também esses sonhos, assim, de me especializar numa área que quase ninguém trabalha ou viajar para o exterior às vezes eram meio inalcançáveis."

A jovem conta que recebeu livros, roupas, perfumes, cursos de inglês e um iPhone . Também viajou para um resort na Bahia com um dos homens que conheceu na plataforma.

Além dos benefícios materiais, relata que os contatos abriram caminhos profissionais. Trabalhando com práticas como fitoterapia, massoterapia e acupuntura, alguns desses homens se tornaram pacientes.

"É literalmente um relacionamento sem as caixas. Tipo, aconteceu isso no meu dia, nossa, estou estressado por causa disso. Vai nas conexões da vida", afirma.

A jovem afirma que as relações sugar que vivenciou não tinham necessariamente o sexo como objetivo principal.

Segundo ela, algumas experiências envolveram intimidade sexual, enquanto outras foram marcadas por conversas, trocas afetivas ou interesses específicos.

A biomédica afirma que uma das experiências mais marcantes foi com um homem interessado em práticas de dominação. Segundo ela, o contato a fez conhecer um universo que não fazia parte de sua rotina e proporcionou aprendizados pessoais.

Ao falar sobre a frequência de relações sexuais em seus encontros, ela afirma que isso ocorreu em uma parcela menor das experiências.

“Sim, sim, já aconteceu. Em um dos encontros, evoluí pra ato, sim, mas digamos aí que 20 a 30% no máximo. É a menor parcela, obviamente."

Ela também diferencia esse tipo de relacionamento de uma troca direta de dinheiro por um encontro sexual, como é o caso da prostituição. "Não é o foco. Se fosse o foco, não seria relacionamento sugar", defende.

Segundo a entrevistada, as relações costumam ser construídas a partir da convivência e do conhecimento mútuo, e os benefícios materiais surgem conforme a conexão entre as pessoas se desenvolve.

A jovem conta que só deixaria a plataforma caso encontre um relacionamento fixo com um daddy.

"Enquanto eu não tiver um relacionamento concreto, para mim não tem sentido sair. Para mim é que nem um aplicativo de namoro, literalmente", completou.

articles.title: US fines Bank of America $1.2bn for money laundering, sanctions violations
articles.summary: The second-largest US bank faces record penalties for failing to comply with money laundering and sanctions laws.
articles.body:
The US Treasury Department has imposed more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America, the second-largest bank in the US, for violating anti-money laundering and sanctions laws.

The fines announced on Tuesday include the third-largest penalty in the department’s history, the US Treasury said in a statement.

“When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire US financial system to significant illicit finance risks,” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.

He added that these “actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law”.

According to the Treasury Department, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a $1.2 billion penalty over the bank’s failure to mitigate and report “priority national security risks, including Chinese Money Laundering Networks and illicit finance along the southwest border”.

The failures identified by FinCEN involved deficiencies related to the bank’s suspicious transaction identification and reporting and customer due diligence processes. According to the statement, “the Bank effectively outsourced to third parties a substantial portion of its proactive detection and reporting obligations”.

“Bank of America failed to timely report to FinCEN over $5 billion dollars in suspicious transactions”, the Treasury said in the statement.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) assessed a $750 million fine, the largest in its history, for the bank’s deficient and ineffective anti-money laundering compliance programme. FinCEN’s $1.2 billion penalty includes credit for the OCC fine.

The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) also announced an $11.6 million settlement agreement over apparent violations of numerous sanctions programmes, including on Iran, Russia, narcotics and global terrorism.

Bank of America agreed to settle 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programmes, and the settlement includes “significant compliance commitments regarding training, testing and audit, and future communication and cooperation with OFAC”.

In the statement, the Treasury said the actions “underscore the importance of effectively complying” with US anti-money laundering and sanctions requirements.

In response, Bank of America said in a statement: “Financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right.”

“We have invested billions of dollars in technology and dedicated thousands of employees to combat financial crime, and our team is far along with and committed to completing the work required to address the issues raised by our regulators.”

articles.title: French AI CEO warns Americans against voting Democrat saying 'you don't want to be France'
articles.summary: Brivael Le Pogam's viral post warned Americans against voting Democrat, saying France's decades of progressive spending led to crushing debt and decline.
articles.body: Brivael Le Pogam, co-founder and self-proclaimed "techno-emperor" of the French AI company Argil, went viral on Tuesday for his X post urging his American followers to not vote for Democrats if they want to avoid his country's fate. "I’m French. I want to talk to Americans who are about to vote Democrat. Not to insult you. To warn you. I come from your future," Le Pogam began his post. He explained that under progressive politicians, France increased public spending to nearly 57% of the country's total GDP in an effort to push free healthcare, free college and a strong welfare system. The results, however, have been dismal. ANDY BESHEAR CALLS SOCIALISM A 'FAILED EXPERIMENT' AS POLL FINDS DEMS VIEW IT MORE FAVORABLY THAN CAPITALISM "Here’s what it looks like from the inside. France hasn’t passed a balanced budget since 1974. Our debt is above 3,300 billion euros. Interest on that debt is becoming one of the biggest items in the national budget. Our hospitals are collapsing despite record funding. Our schools rank lower every year. Young people with degrees can’t afford an apartment in the city they were born in. Our best engineers leave for London, Zurich and San Francisco. And the rich you wanted to tax? They left too, and took the jobs with them," Le Pogam wrote. He warned his followers that France did not vote for decline but faced the repercussions of 50 years' worth of taxes and regulations, encouraging Americans not to go down the same path. DSA-BACKED CANDIDATES ARE WINNING PRIMARIES AND THEIR VISION FOR AMERICA IS VERY DIFFERENT "I love America because it’s the one place on earth where people still believe they can build something from nothing. I came to Silicon Valley as a self-taught kid and it changed my life. That spirit is the most precious thing your country has. Before you vote, ask yourself one question: is the program you’re voting for making America more like America, or more like France? Trust me. You don’t want to be France," Le Pogam ended. Le Pogam's post quickly went viral, being shared by several conservative commentators along with billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman. "An important read on how we keep America from becoming France, from a Frenchman," Ackman wrote. Le Pogam made multiple follow-up posts to his original comments and responded to the accusations that "Democrats aren't socialists" and "America will never be France." He remarked that over the last 25 years, products subsidized by the government, such as healthcare, education and housing, have exploded in cost while goods not funded with government tax dollars, such as phones or software, have only gotten more affordable. I ESCAPED COMMUNISM. AMERICA MUST NOT IGNORE THE URGENT WARNING SIGNS "That's the Trojan horse. It always works the same way. A real problem. A generous-sounding promise. A program that makes things worse. Then the failure of that program becomes the argument for the next one. People who lived under communism in Poland learned to recognize the lie and the mask the lie wears. The lie never presents itself as a lie. It presents itself as compassion," Le Pogam wrote. He added, "In France we are at the end of that road. Debt we can never repay. Young people who can't afford a home. Our best people leaving. And every few years our cities burn. Nobody voted for this. They voted for one more generous promise, fifty years in a row. If you're a Republican, share this with the Democrat in your life. Not to win an argument. To start a conversation. If you're a Democrat, I'm not asking you to switch teams. I'm asking you to look at the pattern. Wherever the state took over, life became unaffordable. Don't fix the failures of government with more government. Stay American. Ask for less state, not more." In a comment to Fox News Digital, Le Pogam stood by his comments, saying the reception "has been very positive overall." He also threw his support behind the Republican Party. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "In general, I support the Republicans. I believe their platform is currently the one that better protects the dynamism, individual freedom, and entrepreneurial spirit that make America unique — and that Europe (especially France) has largely abandoned," Le Pogam said.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Spy chief's grim warning' and 'tiger's victim was child actor'
articles.summary: Wednesday's papers are dominated by coverage of a speech given by the MI5 chief and the death of a man in a tiger enclosure.
articles.body:
Many of the front pages focus on the head of MI5 warning that Russia poses the biggest threat to the UK. "Red alert" is the Daily Mirror's headline.

The Daily Express highlights that Sir Ken McCallum said that "Russian trolls" alleged to have influenced the Brexit debate a decade ago will be "delighted" to be front page news once again, after being mentioned by the prime minister in a recent interview.

The Express warns that the UK must not "play into the hands of Putin". The Brexit referendum is the Daily Telegraph's focus as well, saying Sir Ken insisted the result was not in dispute.

According to the Times, the Chancellor John Healey is to use his Budget later this month to announce what's described as a "tax crackdown" on online retailers.

Under the plans online marketplaces such as Amazon, eBay and Temu will for the first time be made responsible for collecting tax owed by retailers selling on their platforms.

The Financial Times also looks ahead to the Budget, reporting that the Chancellor and the prime minister have been holding meetings with Britain's bosses in an attempt to calm any nerves.

Andy Burnham is said to have reassured executives after telling them he wanted to run the most "pro-business country in the world".

The Daily Telegraph reports that leading dementia experts are calling for ministers to lift, what's described as, an "NHS block" on breakthrough Alzheimer's drugs . Lecanemab and donanemab were licensed in Britain in 2024, but the health watchdog Nice ruled that the benefits didn't justify their cost.

A government spokesperson has said decisions on whether to approve drugs for routine use were taken independently.

And most of the papers mark London's oldest restaurant, Rules in Covent Garden, being donated to the National Trust.

The Daily Telegraph notes that the move will protect the restaurant, which was a favourite of Charles Dickens, against redevelopment. The Times says the nation has been " served a dining institution ".

Under the headline "red alert", The Daily Mirror reports on his warning that Russia is the "number one threat" to UK security. Danger exists in the form of "sabotage, arson, AI, bio-weapons, coercion and violence", with the MI5 chief comparing the situation to that the which existed after 9/11.

articles.title: Great Wolf Lodge horror as mom accused of killing husband and toddler inside hotel room
articles.summary: Metallica Rose Harrison allegedly stabbed her husband and toddler at a Great Wolf Lodge in Pennsylvania before telling responders about her "happy family."
articles.body: A Pennsylvania mom is accused of stabbing her husband and toddler to death inside a Great Wolf Lodge hotel room before telling emergency responders she was supposed to have her "happy family." Metallica Rose Harrison, 27, of Towanda, faces two counts of criminal homicide after police discovered her husband, Charles Harrison, and their 3-year-old son dead inside the resort Monday, according to a criminal complaint reviewed by Fox News Digital. "It wasn't supposed to end like this. I was supposed to have my happy family. That's what I envisioned since I was a child," Harrison allegedly said during the ambulance ride to a hospital. TEXAS MOTHER FACING CAPITAL MURDER CHARGES AFTER ALLEGEDLY SHOOTING HER TWO SONS TO DEATH Pocono Township police responded to room 2030 at the resort in Scotrun around 3:13 p.m. Oct. 12 after Harrison called dispatchers seeking help dying, according to the affidavit. Officers encountered Harrison at the doorway with bleeding cuts on her wrist and puncture wounds around her neck. She told them she wanted to be with her husband and son, investigators wrote. Inside, police found Charles Harrison with multiple stab wounds to his chest. The couple’s son, identified in the complaint by his initials, appeared to have a single stab wound to his chest. Harrison was taken to St. Luke’s Hospital’s Monroe Campus in Stroudsburg for treatment. FORMER CORRECTIONS OFFICER ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE, FORCING KIDS TO HELP "Every day, I work so hard. To be the best person, the best mother, the best wife," she allegedly told emergency responders before lamenting how things had ended. Investigators found a large kitchen knife on the bathroom floor and a smaller knife on the bathroom sink, according to the affidavit. Both had teal green handles, and resort staff told police they were not the type of knives kept by the lodge. Several medication bottles were also scattered throughout the room, investigators wrote. The family had checked into the resort Sept. 21 and extended their reservation on Oct. 5, with checkout scheduled for Oct. 13, according to information police obtained from lodge security. NORTH DAKOTA MOM STABS HER 2 CHILDREN TO DEATH IN 'HORRIFIC' KILLING THAT LEFT COPS TRAUMATIZED: OFFICIALS Surveillance video showed all three family members entering their room around 6:53 p.m. Sunday. Later that night, Harrison and her husband visited the arcade before returning to the room around 11:22 p.m., the affidavit states. Monroe County District Attorney Michael Mancuso described the complaint as "disturbing reading" and said investigators were continuing to gather evidence. "The investigation continues as we gather further evidence shedding light on the circumstances surrounding this horrendous situation," Mancuso wrote in a statement. He thanked township officers, Pennsylvania State Police forensic investigators and the county coroner’s office for their work, describing the room as a "complex double homicide scene." Mancuso emphasized that Harrison is presumed innocent and that prosecutors must prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. Police described the deaths as an isolated domestic tragedy and said there was no threat to the community. Great Wolf Lodge told Fox News Digital it was "deeply saddened and heartbroken" by the deaths and was cooperating with investigators. "It was an isolated family incident, and we’re cooperating fully with local law enforcement as they conduct their investigation," the resort said in a statement. "Our thoughts are with the family and loved ones of those affected." A resort spokesperson said responding officers quickly determined there was no ongoing security concern.

articles.title: Colombia peace tribunal charges ex-FARC members with anti-Indigenous crimes
articles.summary: The former rebels are accused of abuses such as torture, murder and the displacement of Indigenous communities.
articles.body:
Colombia’s transitional justice system, established to address crimes committed during the country’s decades-long civil conflict , has indicted several former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), formerly the country’s largest rebel group.

A group of 10 ex-rebels were charged on Tuesday with alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity between 1996 and 2016.

The Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP), the transitional justice tribunal, said that the accused had carried out crimes of torture, murder and forced displacement against five Indigenous groups in southeast Colombia.

“Today we are delivering justice to the most forgotten peoples of a segregated Colombia,” JEP magistrate Catalina Diaz said.

She explained that FARC commanders had ordered subordinates to plant landmines on Indigenous territory and ruin ecosystems the tribes relied on for survival.

“These people have had their basic right to exist compromised,” Diaz added.

The indictment is the latest example of Colombia’s efforts to reckon with the abuses and violence of a civil conflict that lasted for more than half a century, resulting in severe rights abuses .

Since the 1960s, left-wing rebels, government security forces, criminal networks and government-aligned right-wing paramilitaries have clashed over efforts to control territory and shape the country’s power structure.

Indigenous communities and activists continue to face violent attacks in Colombia today. Continued fighting has also led to an ever-growing death toll.

A 2022 report from Colombia’s Truth Commission found that 450,664 people were killed between 1985 and 2018 as a result of the conflict. An additional 121,768 people were forcibly disappeared.

Indigenous activists and community leaders hailed JEP’s decision on Tuesday as an acknowledgement that their communities were targeted.

“For the first time, the Colombian state recognises that [armed groups] did not just kill individuals,” said Yhon Jairo Figueroa, a leader of the Koreguaje tribe. “But they attempted to kill the knowledge, the language, the territory.”

Three of those accused are also former members of the last secretariat of the FARC, which reached a peace deal with the government in 2016 that included disarmament.

Critics of the deal and its implementation say that many of those responsible for abuses have escaped accountability. Some FARC fighters who refused to accept the agreement have since formed splinter groups that continue to fight in the conflict.

The 2016 deal ultimately granted the former rebels 10 seats in Colombia’s Congress to address the FARC’s political concerns.

One of the suspects indicted Tuesday was Julian Gallo, who served eight years as a senator under that deal.

The JEP, for its part, can impose only non-prison penalties. Last year, for instance, it sentenced seven ex-FARC members accused of kidnapping to eight years of reparations, including landmine clearing and helping to find missing persons.

Separately, JEP also sentenced former military members to reparation work for their involvement in the killing and disappearances of civilians, who were then tallied as rebels in government records. Those systemic misrepresentations became known as the “false positives” scandal.

But critics warn that threats to JEP’s existence loom under Colombia’s newly inaugurated far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella .

Allies of de la Espriella have proposed a nearly 17 percent cut to JEP’s funding for fiscal year 2027. Such budget reductions are set to be weighed by Colombia’s Congress this month.

Before taking office in August, de la Espriella served as a defence lawyer, in some cases representing right-wing paramilitaries. He has criticised the JEP, accusing it of issuing lenient sentences.

articles.title: Jamaica accepts first flight of third-country deportations from US
articles.summary: Opposition leaders in Jamaica question why the deportation deal with the Trump White House has not been made public.
articles.body:
The Caribbean country of Jamaica has received its first third-country deportations from the United States, as part of an expanding set of international agreements under President Donald Trump.

On Tuesday, 22 deportees from the US arrived at Norman Manley International Airport in Kingston, Jamaica.

Media reports indicate they were subsequently boarded onto a bus and taken to an undisclosed location.

Such deportations – which often involve non-citizens who have no ties to their destinations – have faced widespread condemnation from human rights groups and advocates who have questioned their legality.

But Jamaica is among a growing number of countries to accept third-country deportations, as part of Trump’s effort to implement the largest mass deportation campaign in US history.

At least 35 countries have entered into third-country deportation agreements with the US, according to Third Country Deportation Watch, an advocacy project affiliated with the groups Refugees International and Human Rights First.

The Washington Post reported last month that the Trump administration has earmarked roughly $410m to support such efforts.

Jamaica signed a bilateral memorandum of understanding in June to receive third-country deportations. Under the plan, Jamaica will transfer any deportees to their home countries or other destinations after their arrival.

The country’s government has also pledged not to accept any deportees with criminal records.

“The government reiterates that this is a transit arrangement intended to facilitate the return of Third Country Nationals to their country of origin or other receiving countries,” Jamaica’s Ministry of National Security and Peace and its Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade said in a joint statement.

It added that care for the deportees will be supported by the International Organization for Migration, a United Nations organisation.

“The arrangement will not be funded by the Government of Jamaica,” the joint statement added.

Opposition leaders in Jamaica, however, spoke out against the deportation, framing the deal as a threat to the island’s security. They also questioned why the agreement had not been debated publicly.

“Jamaicans are being asked to trust a secret document that touches their security, their communities and their public services,” said Fitz Jackson, the opposition spokesperson on national security.

In response to Jackson’s statement, Foreign Minister Kamina Johnson Smith argued that any questions about the deportation deal “have all been answered”. She also indicated that the US has not agreed to make the deal public.

“As I explained before, some countries have agreed to receive criminals, we have not,” she wrote on social media.

“Some countries have had their agreements made public, but our partner has not agreed for this one to be.”

Legal challenges against the third-country deportations are ongoing in the US, where advocates have argued that deportees are being removed from the country without due process of law, the constitutional right to a fair hearing.

Critics have also argued that third-country deportations sometimes send immigrants to countries where they may face danger.

Some of the recipient countries, such as South Sudan, are in the midst of ongoing conflict or have faced accusations of serious human rights abuses.

Opponents have even said the third-country deportations are being used as a backdoor method for circumventing court protection orders .

Such orders may prohibit the US government from returning certain immigrants to their home countries, for fear of violence and persecution.

But by sending immigrants to third countries, critics say the Trump administration avoids violating such protection orders – though in some cases, the third country has then returned the deportee to the country identified in the US protection order.

In a February report by Democrats on the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee, one official said anonymously that the purpose of such far-flung deportations was to instil fear.

“The point is that the administration can threaten people that they will literally be dropped in the middle of nowhere,” the official said. “The point is to scare people.”

images.caption: Costa Rican authorities receive a flight carrying 25 third-country deportees from the US on April 11, 2026 [Mayela Lopez/Reuters]

articles.title: Florida executes inmate who killed cellmate because he wanted death penalty
articles.summary: A Florida inmate who strangled his cellmate in the hopes of receiving the death penalty rather than spend his remaining years in prison was executed on Tuesday.
articles.body: A Florida man who said he murdered his cellmate in the hopes of securing a death sentence was executed on Tuesday. James Robertson, 63, died after receiving a three-drug injection at Florida State Prison. He was pronounced dead about 10 minutes after the lethal injection was administered. Robertson declined to give a final statement when asked if he had any last words. "Nah, I’m straight," he responded. TWO FLORIDA INMATES DIE IN RARE DOUBLE EXECUTION AFTER SCOTUS DENIES STAYS Robertson's execution was a stark contrast to the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee two weeks ago, when she survived two doses of pentobarbital and was rushed to the hospital. Pike has since been released from the hospital and returned to prison. "Florida has a sound lethal injection process and protocol," Jordan Kirkland, a state Department of Corrections spokesperson, said at a news conference ahead of the execution. While he could not speak about Tennessee’s lethal injection protocol, Kirkland said Florida would make sure its process was "humane and dignified." Florida injects death row inmates with a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart when they are put to death, according to the state Department of Corrections. Robertson had pleaded guilty to first-degree murder for strangling his cellmate, Frank Hart, as he was sleeping in 2008. He waived all appeals and told investigators that he killed the man so he would be given the death penalty and not have to live out the rest of his days behind bars. Hart was killed just eight days before he was set to be released, according to his daughter, Rebecca Hart, who emphasized that her father was not only a piece of Robertson’s story. "When someone you love is taken from you in such a violent way, the world keeps moving, even when a part of yours feels like it has stopped," she told reporters outside the prison. "Other people go on with their lives, but you carry your loss into every tomorrow." Hart was sentenced to prison in 2003 following a sexual battery conviction. Robertson was only 17 years old when he was sent to prison in 1980 for burglary and assault. Additional convictions for escape, battery and weapons offenses extended his prison sentence. Florida was initially scheduled to execute two people on Tuesday, but Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis withdrew a death warrant last week for William Lee Thompson, 74, who was sentenced to death for his role in the 1976 kidnapping and killing of 23-year-old Sally Ivester. He was convicted of first-degree murder, kidnapping and sexual battery in connection with Ivester's death. DeSantis did not provide a reason for stopping the execution but had temporarily stayed the execution last month pending a psychiatric evaluation amid concerns about Thompson's mental competency and deteriorating health. His attorneys said he has dementia and failing health and want him transferred to a medical facility. This was the first time DeSantis withdrew a death warrant. Thompson will remain on death row, and a new death warrant could be signed in the future. DeSantis is the third Florida governor to sign a death warrant for Thompson. Former Govs. Bob Graham and Bob Martinez each scheduled executions for Thompson in the 1980s, but he avoided the electric chair, the state's method of execution at the time, after years of appeals and stays. In July, Florida executed two prisoners in one day, the first time a state has done so in nearly a decade. Florida has accelerated its pace of executions amid a flurry of death warrants signed by DeSantis since 2025. The governor oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more than any other Florida governor in a single year since the death penalty was reinstated in 1976, accounting for approximately 40% of the U.S. total for 2025. TEXAS EXECUTES JAMAAL HOWARD DESPITE CONCERNS OVER LETHAL INJECTION DRUG USED IN FAILED TENNESSEE EXECUTION CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Last year, 47 executions were carried out nationwide, the highest annual total since 2009. Florida has carried out more than half of the 31 total executions in the country so far this year. Robertson was the Sunshine State's 17th execution of 2026, with two more already scheduled, not including Thompson. William Reaves, 77, who was convicted of fatally shooting a deputy in 1986, is scheduled to be executed Oct. 20. Jesse Guardado, 64, is scheduled to be executed Nov. 5 for robbing and killing a woman to buy drugs in 2004. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trump Energy Department issues emergency order to prevent blackouts across 13 states amid unusual October heat
articles.summary: The Department of Energy authorized PJM Interconnection to tap backup power as unseasonably warm October temperatures strain the grid across 13 states.
articles.body: The Trump administration has issued an emergency order aimed at preventing potential blackouts across 13 states as unseasonably warm October temperatures strain the electrical grid serving more than 60 million Americans. The Department of Energy authorized PJM Interconnection, a regional grid operator, to use additional power generation resources as rising electricity demand coincides with scheduled maintenance at power plants and transmission facilities. The order, issued Monday under Section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act, takes effect Tuesday and remains in place through Friday, Oct. 16. It allows certain generating facilities to operate beyond normal restrictions if needed to maintain electricity supplies. WHO PAYS FOR US POWER BOOM? BLUE, RED STATES OFFER STARKLY DIFFERENT WAYS TO LOWER UTILITY BILLS AMID AI SURGE PJM serves all or parts of Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia and Washington, D.C. PJM Interconnection told Fox News Digital it does not expect the emergency conditions to affect everyday customers but warned that rising electricity demand and unpredictable weather patterns are creating new challenges for grid reliability. Jeff Shields, a spokesperson for PJM, said electricity demand is growing faster than new generating capacity can come online, while unpredictable weather is leaving fewer opportunities for critical maintenance and construction. Shields added that planned maintenance periods now present reliability risks that grid operators previously faced primarily during summer and winter. LAWMAKERS TARGET ENERGY AFFORDABILITY THROUGH SWEEPING PERMITTING OVERHAUL IN NEW HOUSE BILL "This order will help ensure millions of American families and businesses across the mid-Atlantic have access to affordable, reliable and secure electricity by making additional power generation, including backup power, available to use as needed," Energy Secretary Chris Wright said. The emergency action comes as temperatures across parts of the Ohio Valley and Mid-Atlantic are expected to climb into the 70s and 80s, increasing electricity demand while some generating facilities and transmission lines remain offline for maintenance. Wright also criticized energy policies under former President Joe Biden, arguing that restrictions on conventional energy production have weakened grid reliability. TRUMP'S EPA REFORMS ARE A HUGE BOOST TO MANUFACTURERS, BUT THERE'S MORE RED TAPE TO CUT: EXPERT The emergency order comes as the Energy Department pursues separate investments to strengthen the nation's electrical infrastructure. DOE recently announced plans to support 84 Tennessee Valley Authority transmission and distribution projects across eight states, representing approximately $581 million in planned investments. The projects, which include $250 million in federal funding, are expected to add roughly 2.5 gigawatts of grid capacity, improve reliability for 2.58 million families and businesses and support approximately 800 jobs. The TVA initiative is separate from the PJM emergency order, and its final funding and regulatory approvals remain pending.
